conventions.convention: Probability measures and counting measures carry their evaluation sigma-algebras; no topology on the space of probability measures is asserted.

The DP base measure is finite and nonzero on a standard Borel space. Zero-base partition cells have mass zero almost surely and are omitted from the positive-parameter Dirichlet vector; one positive cell has mass one.

Counting measures allow repeated points and countably many atoms without a local-finiteness requirement. The PRM independence and Poisson-law requirements apply to finite disjoint families of finite-intensity sets.

Full AC is assumed for normalized-gamma existence and carried through aggregation, posterior updating, prediction, and the examples; it supplies the Countable Choice required by the density interfaces.
The posterior update is a measurable data-indexed version defined at every data vector; its values on prior-predictive null sets are not uniquely forced.
Posterior updating assumes n ≥ 1; the predictive proof also treats n = 0 as the prior predictive case.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. On a standard Borel space with finite nonzero base measure α, there exists an evaluation-measurable random probability measure with law DP(α). Its unnormalized partition increments are independent Gamma(α(A_j),1) variables for positive-base cells and zero almost surely for zero-base cells. The finite-partition laws uniquely determine the DP law.

Assume AC. For G ∼ DP(α) on a standard Borel space with finite nonzero α and conditional sample law G⊗n, n ≥ 1, K(x;·) = DP(α + Σ_i δ_{x_i}) is a measurable data-indexed posterior kernel satisfying disintegration. Its values on prior-predictive null data sets are version choices.

For a finite nonzero base measure α on a standard Borel space, DP(α) denotes the law on evaluation-measurable probability measures having Dirichlet finite-partition distributions after zero-parameter cells are omitted, with those omitted cells assigned mass zero.

Assume AC. If P has a Dirichlet distribution with positive parameters a_j and the coordinate indices are partitioned into nonempty groups I_ℓ, then the grouped sums have Dirichlet parameters b_ℓ = Σ_{j∈I_ℓ} a_j. One group gives the point mass at one.

Assume AC. In the conditionally IID DP model, the chosen one-step predictive version assigns A probability (α(A) + Σ_i 1_A(x_i))/(α(X) + n) for every measurable A and every data vector, with null-data values understood as version choices.
If S is a nonempty at-most-countable set, then (S, P(S)) is a standard Borel space.

seams_checked.note: The DP construction uses the positive-parameter shape-rate Gamma and Dirichlet interfaces. Posterior updating applies Dirichlet-multinomial conjugacy only after omitting zero-base cells with zero counts; impossible ordered patterns have predictive mass zero. Full AC supplies the supplier's Countable Choice hypothesis.

The simplex and local-prior-mass arguments use the actual finite-partition laws with zero-cell conventions. The sieve-tail proof applies the update and predictive law to latent conditionally IID locations, using exchangeability for leave-one-out prediction. AC and finite nonzero base hypotheses are retained; contraction is established through separate mixture arguments.
All four examples cite the discrete-space lemma only to establish standard Borel structure for nonempty finite or countable power-set spaces. They do not import DP conjugacy or predictive claims.
